trial_name.text: Trial AT-301 (also referred to as Trial 1)

citations.quote: Trial AT-301 was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of cefepime-AAI101 (enmetazobactam) compared to piperacillin/tazobactam for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections, including acute pyelonephritis, in adults.

n.text: 1,041 subjects randomized (MITT/safety population 1,034; m-MITT population N=345 cefepime-enmetazobactam and N=333 piperacillin/tazobactam)

result.text: Overall success at Test of Cure occurred in 79.1% (273/345) of the cefepime-enmetazobactam group versus 58.9% (196/333) of the piperacillin/tazobactam group; treatment difference 21.2% (95% CI 14.3, 27.9). Because the lower limit of the 95% CI (14.3%) was above zero and above the prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%, the trial demonstrated both noninferiority and superiority of cefepime-enmetazobactam over piperacillin/tazobactam.

indication.text: Treatment of patients 18 years of age and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible microorganisms: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae complex.

citations.quote: EXBLIFEP® is indicated for the treatment of patients 18 years of age and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis, caused by the following susceptible microorganisms: *Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, *Proteus mirabilis*, and *Enterobacter cloacae* complex.

target_moa.text: Cefepime is a cephalosporin whose bactericidal action results from inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); enmetazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects cefepime from degradation by certain serine beta-lactamases such as ESBL.

citations.quote: The cefepime component of EXBLIFEP is a cephalosporin antibacterial drug. The bactericidal action of cefepime results from the inhibition of cell wall synthesis. Cefepime penetrates the cell wall of most gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria to bind penicillin-binding protein (PBP) targets. Cefepime is stable to hydrolysis by some beta-lactamases, including penicillinases and cephalosporinases
The enmetazobactam component of EXBLIFEP is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects cefepime from degradation by certain serine beta-lactamases such as ESBL.

modality.text: Small molecule combination product: cefepime (a cephalosporin beta-lactam antibacterial) and enmetazobactam (a beta-lactamase inhibitor) for injection.

citations.quote: EXBLIFEP (cefepime and enmetazobactam) for injection is a combination product that contains cefepime, a cephalosporin antibacterial drug, and enmetazobactam, a beta-lactamase inhibitor, for intravenous administration.

key_safety.text: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (≥5%) were transaminases increased (20% vs 20%), bilirubin increased (7% vs 4%), headache (5% vs 2%), and phlebitis/infusion site reactions (5% vs <1%). Treatment was discontinued due to adverse reactions in 3% (13/516) of EXBLIFEP patients versus 2% (10/518) of piperacillin/tazobactam patients. Warnings include hypersensitivity reactions, neurotoxicity, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea.

citations.quote: The most frequently reported adverse reactions (5% or greater) in patients receiving EXBLIFEP were transaminases increased, bilirubin increased, headache, and phlebitis/infusion site reactions. summary.text: NDA 216165 was submitted June 22, 2023 with both Fast Track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designations; the sponsor requested and was granted priority review, with a PDUFA goal date of February 22, 2024. Approval was based on a single Phase 3 noninferiority trial (AT-301) and was not an accelerated approval.

changes.note: Removed the conflicting line-43 'assessor-blinded' citation and replaced it with line 66 of the IntegratedR, which describes the pivotal trial verbatim as 'randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter, noninferiority trial,' eliminating the internal contradiction while keeping the 'double-blind' value grounded (also supported by line 122).

Reconciled the 1041-vs-1034 discrepancy using the disposition table at line 173 of the IntegratedR, which shows 1041 randomized total, MITT/safety = 1034, and m-MITT N=345 (CEF/ENME) and N=333 (pip/tazo); updated text to note MITT/safety=1,034 and cited line 173 plus the m-MITT header at line 181.

The denominators 273/345 and 196/333 are grounded within the field by the line-181 table citation ('Success 273 (79.1) 196 (58.9) 21.2 (14.3, 27.9)' with N=345/N=333 header); retained line 181 in this field.

Corrected the 'exceeded margin / mere noninferiority' wording to state both noninferiority and superiority, grounded in line 178 of the IntegratedR ('The results demonstrated noninferiority and superiority of cefepime-AAI101 to piperacillin/tazobactam in overall response'), and clarified the lower CI limit of 14.3% was above zero and above the -10% margin.
